clue.text: Trees found by mammal when crossing mountain

indicators.note: the mammal-and-when pair straddles the mountain, so it sits across the middle of them

parts.note: a cat is a mammal
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: Some trees are discovered by an animal as it makes its way over a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' reads as a time link in the surface, but it supplies letters; the mammal and that short word sit either side of the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalpa is a genus of ornamental trees with large heart-shaped leaves and long seed pods.

clue.text: An aider in a maze

indicators.note: being in a maze means being confused, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who gave help inside a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AN AIDER rearrange to give the name, and the whole clue also describes her: in Greek myth she gave Theseus the thread that led him out of the Minotaur's labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this princess helped Theseus escape the labyrinth with a ball of thread.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful stretch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hard timber from the tree of that name.

clue.text: Stop at the end of a sentence?

definitions.text: Stop at the end of a sentence?

parts.words: Stop at the end of a sentence?
parts.note: a full stop is the dot that ends a written sentence; the surface suggests halting someone as they finish speaking

explanation.surface: Stopping when a sentence is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: A full stop is one of the symbols used in writing to separate and end sentences; 'Stop' hides that dot.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is one example of the written symbols such as commas and colons that organise text.

clue.text: Plants I found in the middle of Russia

indicators.note: the self is said to be found inside the central part of the country's name
Russia has six letters, so its middle is the pair at its centre

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone discovered certain plants deep in the heart of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: With an even number of letters, a word's middle is the central pair. 'I' is the classic crossword route to the Latin self, and sego is a lily of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: The sego lily is a flowering bulb native to the western United States, so segos are plants.

clue.text: Person needs time going round wine store

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person

indicators.note: turning round means the word for time is read from end to start

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages to walk round a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the time word to EGA. BOD, British slang for a person, is a staple of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar.

clue.text: Guilt of Elizabeth strangling horrible mother-in-law

indicators.note: strangling is gripping round the neck, so the name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

indicators.note: something horrible is ugly and distorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elizabeth is to blame for throttling her dreadful mother-in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges the hyphenated relative to LAMEWORTHIN. 'of' is a link; the hyphens give no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worthy of blame is the state of being culpable for a wrong.

clue.text: Performed as magician and was effective

definitions.meaning: a conjuror who completed an illusion carried out the stunt
an idiom for something that worked or achieved its purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a conjuror carried out the illusion; idiomatically, a remedy that worked brought about the desired result.

clue.text: Cells with entrances blocked by this person

indicators.note: the entrances are obstructed by having the setter put in their middle

parts.note: gates are entrances
this person is the setter, who refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Doorways barred by the speaker hold prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cells' suggests prisons, matching the barred entrances, but the definition is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: Gametes are reproductive cells such as sperm and egg cells.

clue.text: Plant on stone right outside church

indicators.note: the right is placed around the church, standing outside it

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A plant grows on a stone near the correct side of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like a direction (R), but it is a legal claim. The definition is three words: these crusty growths cover rocks and gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichen is a fungus-and-alga growth that commonly encrusts rocks and walls.

clue.text: Old woman has fun collecting foreign money

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the word for fun holds the currency

parts.note: a game is fun or sport
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A grandmother enjoys herself gathering overseas cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The South African currency is a favourite of setters for 'foreign money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandame is an old word for a grandmother or an elderly lady.

clue.text: Tea missed carelessly? Here's a cup of coffee

indicators.note: doing something carelessly leaves things in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who forgot the tea is offered coffee instead.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA MISSED rearranges to the answer; 'Here's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup for strong black coffee, or the coffee served in one.

clue.text: Pa's no hermit — but sadly he doesn't much care for folk!

definitions.text: he doesn't much care for folk!

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Dad may not be a recluse, yet unfortunately he isn't fond of people.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS NO HERMIT rearranges to the answer, using the S of 'Pa's' as a letter; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope dislikes humankind in general.

clue.text: Has old Anne to lose continuously?

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so the second word is removed from the surname

parts.note: Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife
away can mean continuously, as in 'working away'

explanation.surface: Does the old lady Anne keep on losing things?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes AWAY from HATHAWAY. The definition is 'Has old': the answer is an archaic form of has.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the archaic third-person form of the verb have, familiar from the King James Bible.

clue.text: Ordinary iron ship

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An everyday iron-hulled vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry an ordinary is one of the simple basic charges on a shield; this one is a broad horizontal band.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a fess is a horizontal band across a shield, one of the basic charges called ordinaries.

clue.text: Frequent traveller has stories to spin

indicators.note: spinning things round mixes them up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seasoned traveller has tales to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: HAS STORIES rearranges to the answer; the definition fits a flight attendant, who flies constantly for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight attendants travel by plane constantly as part of the job.

clue.text: Bemoan the way Parisians go about

definitions.meaning: to bemoan is to regret or lament
the French word for a street, a way through Paris

explanation.surface: Lament how people in Paris get around.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to regret it; and in French the word is a street, a way Parisians walk along.

clue.text: Matching one bit of money with another I had pocketed

parts.note: a coin is one piece of money

indicators.note: the second coin takes the short form into its pocket, holding it inside

parts.note: a cent is another bit of money
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone has a coin that matches another they kept in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like I, but here it goes with 'bit of money'; the contracted 'I had' is the pocketed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are coincident correspond or occur together in agreement.

clue.text: Active, with 'ankering to go to wild party

parts.note: said with a dropped H, hankering becomes 'ankering, and so hope, a longing, becomes 'ope
a rant is a boisterous merrymaking or wild party

explanation.surface: Someone with a Cockney yearning heads off to a riotous do.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ankering' signals a dropped H, so the synonym loses its H too, Cockney-style. A rant in Scottish use is a boisterous spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means producing an effect, working, in operation.

clue.text: Old warriors encroached, half hidden

indicators.note: with half the word hidden from view, only its front half remains

parts.note: impinged means encroached

explanation.surface: Ancient fighters advanced on territory while partly concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPINGED has eight letters; 'half hidden' keeps only the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment of warriors in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Fortification soldier preferred

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
pet means favourite, as in a pet subject

explanation.surface: The defensive wall a soldier liked best.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall or earth bank on a rampart.

clue.text: Engagement in Times? Hurray!

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words Times and Hurray as they run together

explanation.surface: An engagement announced in the Times newspaper: cheers!
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tiMES Hurray. The engagement is mechanical, as when gear teeth interlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth are said to be in mesh when they interlock and engage.

clue.text: School nurse is a petty critic

definitions.meaning: a school nurse checks pupils' hair for the eggs of head lice
someone who finds fault over trivial details

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, one who removes head-lice eggs from hair; figuratively, a pedant fussing over trivial faults.

clue.text: Walk with energy into square

indicators.note: the energy is put into the middle of the word for square

parts.note: trad, short for traditional, means conventional or square
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Stroll briskly into a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts E inside TRAD; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to walk or step on something.

clue.text: Vandalism in the era of the wooden shoe?

parts.note: a sabot is a clog carved from wood
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Was there property damage back when everyone wore clogs?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the folk tale that the word comes from workers throwing their wooden shoes into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction of property or plans.

clue.text: In bar, look for two characters swapping positions

indicators.note: two letters of the verb change places, so the consonants third and fifth trade spots

parts.note: to expect is to look for or anticipate

explanation.surface: In a pub, someone waits for two people to change seats.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXPECT the P and C trade places. 'bar' is the preposition meaning but, not a pub; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, both mean apart from or excluding.

clue.text: Somewhere up on the mountain most chilly

indicators.note: most of the word means all of it except the final letter

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: High up on the peak it is coldest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims the last letter from COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a pass or saddle between two mountain peaks.

clue.text: Characteristic act that may offend some spectators?

definitions.meaning: a trait, as in a mean or stubborn element of character

definitions.text: act that may offend some spectators?
definitions.meaning: running naked across a sports field in front of the crowd

explanation.definitionFit: A trait in someone's nature, as in a cruel vein; and a naked dash across a pitch that shocks a crowd.

clue.text: Barren time — suffer defeat coming back in

indicators.note: the reversed verb goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the verb for suffering defeat is read backwards

parts.note: to lose is to suffer defeat

explanation.surface: A bleak period when you are beaten on your return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the verb for suffering defeat into ESOL. 'Barren' is the adjective, describing bleak land.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate land is bleak, empty and lifeless.
